subject: Marketplace pricing accordion + channel certification requirements
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@aperturelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace pricing accordion + channel certification requirements

Hi Karthik / Camila —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aperture is excited about Redwood’s latency profile for inference, and we want to kick off the private offer path for our pilot across AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace. A couple of open items from our side before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Pricing flexibility: we need a mechanism to start at a promotional list price for H1, then step up in H2 based on usage triggers (an "accordion" style schedule). Can the private offer support two-phase pricing with automated mid-term SKU repricing?

2) Channel margin & certification: Aperture requires that any reseller we work through be certified and receive a clear margin schedule. Procurement asked for a channel certification checklist and evidence that reseller credits will be passed through (not retained by the marketplace).

3) Evidence for audit: they also need documentation for how overage credits and reserved capacity credits are routed in invoicing (we're attaching our MAAP requirements).

Can you outline the options and share a sample channel pass-through waterfall? We aim to present a single-sheet to our CFO by next Friday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Emily

--
Emily Zhao
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Aperture Labs
emily.zhao@aperturelabs.com
+1-415-555-0136

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@aperturelabs.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing accordion + channel certification requirements

Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then an ask for a couple of clarifying points: 

- Two-phase pricing: yes. We support private-offer payloads that map multiple SKU rows with date-ranged price rules; we can automate an H1->H2 transition via trigger dates or usage thresholds. We typically recommend date-based gating for accounting simplicity.

- Channel margins: we can produce a pass-through waterfall that shows list price -> marketplace fee -> reseller margin -> net to Redwood. The catch: some marketplaces (AWS) deduct fees pre-passback which changes perceived margin. We will provide both "gross-to-net" and "passback-forward" views.

- Audit evidence: we can provide sample invoice mappings and the channel certification checklist you asked for.

Clarifying ask: 
1) Is the Accordion triggered by absolute usage (tokens/month) or by spoiling a spend band (e.g., $250k TCV triggers step)?
2) Do you expect the reseller to invoice Aperture directly (pass-through) or be paid by the marketplace and then pay Aperture/reseller? This affects which party we need to certify.

I'll draft a one-page waterfall and attach an initial channel-margin proposal and the checklist; Camila and Lauren will review for ops/finance alignment. If you can confirm the two points above, we'll aim to have a proposed doc by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Karthik
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1-510-555-0199

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@aperturelabs.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: 2026-06-21T14:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing accordion + channel certification requirements

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick reply. Answers below: 

1) Accordion trigger: prefer spend-band ($) trigger tied to quarterly committed spend rather than raw tokens — finance wants predictable revenue windows.
2) Reseller flow: Aperture wants the certified reseller to be the counterparty to Aperture (i.e., reseller invoices Aperture). Marketplace pays reseller; reseller must provide documentation that they passed credits to Aperture.

Procurement has also asked for a clause that ensures any marketplace surcharges (taxes/marketplace fees) are visually separated on the invoice so our accounting team can validate pass-through.

One more ask — can you include an example where we model a 12% reseller margin, 8% marketplace fee, and a 15% promotional discount in H1 so we can see net revenue to Redwood and net cost to Aperture under three scenarios (low/expected/high usage)? If you can put that into a simple spreadsheet we can review with finance, that would be perfect.

I'll attach the MAAP requirements PDF (see attached) and loop in procurement to review the waterfall once you share it.

Best,
Emily

--
Emily Zhao
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Aperture Labs

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@aperturelabs.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, procurement@aperturelabs.com
Date: 2026-06-22T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace pricing accordion + channel certification requirements

Emily / procurement team —

Attached: RDW-channel-margin-proposal-v1.xlsx (simple waterfall with low/expected/high usage tabs) and our channel certification checklist. Highlights: 

- Modeling assumptions included on the cover tab (12% reseller margin, 8% marketplace fee, 15% H1 promo). We show net-to-Aperture and net-to-Redwood across three anchor TCV bands.
- Accordion implementation options: (A) Date-bound: H1 promotional price active 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31, H2 list price reverts automatically 2027-01-01. (B) Spend-band: we can implement a usage trigger but the marketplace requires the private-offer to include reconciliation notes; this adds an additional invoicing reconciliation step. We recommend Date-bound unless you require precise spend gating.
- Pass-through evidence: we included an example invoice mapping and language you can use in the reseller contract to require proof of credit pass-through (sample clause in the checklist).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Aperture to confirm accordion type (date-bound preferred by Redwood).
2) Aperture procurement to confirm reseller identity for certification (name + tax id).
3) Redwood to open private-offer draft for AWS and GCP once reseller is confirmed; expected lead time varies (AWS ~5 business days, GCP ~7-10 business days after all artifacts are provided).

If that works I'll convert the spreadsheet into a single-sheet summary for your CFO and loop in legal to draft the reseller pass-through clause.

Thanks — Karthik

--

- RDW-channel-margin-proposal-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: waterfalls + scenarios)
